As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
18. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The pecuniary damages or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which she had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by her in the accident.

The non- pecuniary or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed which includes the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of MACT Case No. 357/2022 (FIR no. 294/2020) Sachin Kumar v. Md. Vasim & Anr.
Page no. 8 of 14 money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where she was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate her or to put her almost in the same place or position where she could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

sentences.text: Ld. Counsel for insurance company submits that driver of the motorcycle was under the influence of alcohol as proved by R2W1 Dr. Bandita Rani Roy.
Therefore, Insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation to petitioner.
26. R2W1 has simply deposed that petitioner was found under Alcohol influence in breathing as mentioned in MLC no.2068.
However, no blood sample was taken to ascertain alcohol content in the blood of petitioner.
No slip of BAC Test has been placed on record.
Therefore, no material is available on record to ascertain the content of alcohol in the blood stream of petitioner at the relevant time.
Moreover, the petitioner was not driving the motorcycle at the time of accident.
He was the pillion rider.
Therefore, it is irrelevant whether the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol or not.
The insurance company has failed to prove that the driver of the motorcycle was drunken at the time of accident.
27. Respondent No. 1 Driver/ Owner of the offending car is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, since the offending car was insured with respondent no. 2 at the time of accident, therefore, respondent no. 2/ Insurance Company is liable to indemnify R1 in respect of above liability.
As such, Respondent no. 2/ Insurance company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Respondent no. 2/ Insurance Company is directed to MACT Case No. 357/2022 (FIR no. 294/2020) Sachin Kumar v. Md. Vasim & Anr.
